The project area is presently served by a combined sewer system with a single conduit used to carry both sanitary sewage and rainfall runoff. As part of the project improvements it is proposed that a separate sewage collection system be constructed with the existing sewer system then being utilized for storm drainage purposes only. The sewage collection system shown connects back into the combined sewer system at several locations at the project boundaries until such time as further extensions can be made. In some instances, existing sewers which are not connected to drainage inlets will be maintained as part of the sanitary sewer system. House services now connected to the combined system will be abandoned and re-built or adjusted as required for connection to the separate sanitary sewer system. In clearance areas existing service connections will be plugged as part of project demolition.
3. Storm Drainage:
The schematic layout of the project storm drainage system is shown on Figure 3, Exhibit 7. As noted previously the existing combined sewer system is proposed to serve the project as the storm drainage system.
Certain modifications and improvements of the existing sewer system are proposed to provide carrying compatible with present design criteria:
A 48" diameter relief storm sewer is proposed by the Richmond Metropolitan Authority (RMA) from near the intersection of Lakeview and Shields Avenues to Swan Lake due to inadequate capacity of the existing 66" diameter conduit.
A 30" diameter relief storm sewer is proposed along Allen Avenue from near Powhatan Street to Colorado Avenue due to inadequate capacity of the existing 42" diameter conduit in this reach.
c. Additional catch basins and relatively short storm sewers are proposed at various locations due to street closures, street improvements or new street locations.
4. Water Distribution System:
Figure 4, Exhibit 7 illustrates the schematic layout of the water distribution system for the project area.
The existing water distribution system in the project area is generally adequate for both basic water consumption and fire protection purposes. Minor modification and additions to the existing system are required to meet the objectives of the Redevelopment and Conservation Plan.
a. The relocation of Lakeview Avenue between Lombardy and Harrison will necessitate the relocation of a 24" and 20" transmission mains.
